taxon.note: Scientific and common names (and USDA symbol, where given) as the spec's authors wrote them, and the genus the scientific name is written in.

growth_form.note: The growth form the spec's authors chose from the plant's habit.

growth.note: The growth plan (years, step, keyframes) chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

variants.note: The environments, conditions and seeds chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

taxon.family.note: WCVP v16's family for the accepted name.

taxon.plant_name_id.note: WCVP v16's plant_name_id for the accepted species the name resolves to (the accepted name).

traits.height_typical_m.note: A model estimate (confidence medium), as no source read gives it: flowering scapes 5 cm to 30 cm high, as in the photos.

traits.life_span.note: Abrams vol. 2 (1944) p. 176, Caltha leptosepala: glabrous succulent perennial.

traits.woodiness.note: Abrams vol. 2 (1944) p. 175, Caltha: fleshy perennial herbs.

traits.leaf_habit.note: A model estimate (confidence high), as no source read gives it: the leaves die back each winter under the snow.

traits.rosette.note: Abrams vol. 2 (1944) p. 176, Caltha leptosepala: the stems scapose, the leaves from the base.

traits.cauline_leaves.note: Abrams vol. 2 (1944) p. 176, Caltha leptosepala: stems scapose and 1-flowered or bearing a solitary leaf or bract at the node.

traits.leaf_shape.note: Abrams vol. 2 (1944) p. 176, Caltha leptosepala: leaves cordate, varying from oblong-ovate to ovate-orbicular, longer than broad.

traits.leaf_margin.note: Abrams vol. 2 (1944) p. 176, Caltha leptosepala: repand-dentate to coarsely crenate.

traits.leaf_hairs.note: Abrams vol. 2 (1944) p. 176, Caltha leptosepala: glabrous.

traits.leaf_length_m.note: A model estimate (confidence medium), as no source read gives it: blades 3 cm to 10 cm long; Abrams (1944 p. 175) gives the related C. biflora's blades 5-8 cm broad.

traits.leaf_width_m.note: A model estimate (confidence medium), as no source read gives it: blades 2 cm to 7 cm wide, a little narrower than long (Abrams 1944 p. 176: longer than broad).

traits.petiole_length_m.note: A model estimate (confidence medium), as no source read gives it: petioles 4 cm to 15 cm long, as in the photos; Abrams (1944 p. 175) calls C. biflora's long-petioled.

traits.inflorescence.note: Abrams vol. 2 (1944) p. 176, Caltha leptosepala: the stems 1-flowered or usually 2-flowered; drawn as a two-flowered cyme.

traits.perianth.note: Abrams vol. 2 (1944) p. 175, Caltha: sepals petaloid, large, deciduous; petals none: drawn as one loose series of tepals.

traits.perianth_parts.note: Abrams vol. 2 (1944) p. 176, Caltha leptosepala: sepals 6-12.

traits.tepal_length_m.note: A model estimate (confidence medium), as no source read gives it: sepals 1 cm to 2 cm long, as in the photos.

traits.flower_size_m.note: A model estimate (confidence medium), as no source read gives it: open flowers 2.5 cm to 4 cm across, as in the photos.

traits.flower_colour.note: Abrams vol. 2 (1944) p. 176, Caltha leptosepala: sepals white, varying from oblong-obovate to oblong-linear; sRGB by eye from the photos.

traits.anther_colour.note: Stamens a yellow boss; sRGB by eye, set by hand from iNaturalist photos (observations 234971859, 173262810, 870944, 59545751, 9328, 368257400, 366410234, 13780174): the sources read give no count or measure.

traits.fruit_type.note: Abrams vol. 2 (1944) p. 175, Caltha: fruit follicles, dehiscent on the ventral suture.

traits.fruitlets.note: Abrams vol. 2 (1944) p. 175, Caltha: carpels several to many: a head of follicles.

traits.fruit_size_m.note: Abrams vol. 2 (1944) p. 176, Caltha leptosepala: follicles somewhat diverging when ripe, 12-13 mm. long, short-stipitate.

traits.flowering_months.note: Abrams vol. 2 (1944) p. 176, Caltha leptosepala: June-July.

traits.fruiting_months.note: A model estimate (confidence medium), as no source read gives it: follicles ripe in August and September.

appearance.note: By eye, from the photos the traits cite: a low tuft of glossy, heart-shaped, scalloped leaves on long stalks, with leafless stalks each bearing one or two white, many-sepalled flowers with yellow centres. The basal leaves' petiole share is set by hand from the leaf and petiole lengths the traits give, as no rule sets a rosette leaf's.

generator.params.note: Set by hand for white marsh marigold from its sources and the photos the traits cite: the herb program's structure (stems, nodes, basal leaves, how the flowers are borne). The rest of its growth comes from the library's rules for the form. Not fitted to measurements.

allometry.note: 0.15 m tall at 3 years in the open, within its sources' range, as grown. Replace with measured data before calling this species calibrated.

sources.title: Project After contributors: hand-set species values
sources.licence: project contribution under the repository's terms

provenance.notes: Procedural proxy added for the Mount Rainier subalpine meadow scene (Paradise, 2026-10-19): sizes and forms from Abrams (vols. 2 to 4) and the Range Plant Handbook where it treats the species, counts and colours from iNaturalist photos.
